name: MT-Bench-101
intro: MT-Bench-101 是面向大语言模型多轮对话细粒度能力的英文基准。它从真实对话和教育心理学归纳三层能力分类，以 GPT-4 生成并经五名标注员全票筛选，最终发布 13 项任务中的 1,388 个对话和 4,208 个轮次。
org: Alibaba Group, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory
build_method: 真实对话与教育心理学归纳能力；GPT-4 生成；五名标注员全票筛选
metric: GPT-4 逐轮评分（1–10）；对话最低分；任务均值；13 任务宏平均（论文）
eval_feature: 黄金上下文；任务专属 LLM-as-a-Judge；分层聚合
scale: 1,388 个对话；4,208 个轮次；固定评测实现构造 3,615 个评测项
build_method_en: Ability induction from real dialogues and educational psychology; GPT-4 generation; unanimous five-annotator curation
eval_feature_en: Golden context; task-specific LLM-as-a-Judge; hierarchical aggregation
intro_en: MT-Bench-101 is an English benchmark for fine-grained multi-turn dialogue abilities of large language models. It derives a three-tier ability taxonomy from real dialogues and educational psychology, generates candidates with GPT-4, and retains only items unanimously approved by five annotators, yielding 1,388 dialogues and 4,208 turns across 13 tasks.

drawio_review_note: Evidence was reconciled against arXiv:2402.14762v3 (ACL 2024), the official mtbench101/mt-bench-101 repository at commit bc18b3e2c18c99164e11528f1a79c92083db5953, and the authors' OpenCompass fork/default mtbench101 branch at commit da7b1c3a007efea1dcca985a242e13a0ba51abd1. The released mtbench101.jsonl object has SHA-256 1a1e433acf7e2ef013b5001b60fd8e48bc3e4202460727e25b2ea8575aae7d80 and is public under Apache-2.0. Construction follows Sections 3.1–3.4 and the appendices. The authors analyze ShareGPT/RealChat-style human–LLM dialogues together with educational-psychology concepts, then define three top-level abilities (Perceptivity, Adaptability, Interactivity), seven second-level abilities (Memory, Understanding, Interference, Rephrasing, Reflection, Reasoning, Questioning), and 13 task codes (CM, AR, SI, TS, CC, CR, FR, SC, SA, MR, GR, IC, PI). Task-specific GPT-4 generation combines a uniform initial instruction, unique rules, and handcrafted examples over 30 topics with at least 10 distinct topics per task. The paper says more than 1,000 candidates are generated for each task; it does not publish an exact grand total. Five annotators screen every candidate and retention requires unanimous approval. The documented criteria enforce task rules and topic diversity, remove keyword-only near-duplicates, exclude real-time or post-2022 knowledge, and reject commonsense errors, offensive content, and personally identifying information. Candidate rejection counts, annotator recruitment details, and a separate adjudication protocol are not published, so the graph records that boundary instead of inventing a retry loop or majority-vote acceptance. Direct inspection of the pinned English JSONL confirms 1,388 dialogues, 4,208 history turns, unique IDs 1 through 1,388, 13 task values, and two to seven turns per dialogue. Each row has exactly task, id, and history; every history element contains user and bot text. One exact duplicate history occurs in task SI at IDs 1138 and 1142. No Chinese release was found, so the prior English-and-Chinese catalog label was corrected to English only. The official README still marks its leaderboard as work in progress, so paper result tables are not presented as a live leaderboard. Evaluation follows the golden-context protocol: curated prior turns are supplied and only the newest model response is generated/scored, preventing self-generated history drift. Direct evaluation begins at turn two for FR, CR, AR, SA, SC, and CM; their 593 dialogues each lose one first-turn item. CC, GR, IC, MR, PI, SI, and TS are evaluated from turn one. Thus the fixed implementation constructs 4,208 − 593 = 3,615 evaluation items. The task-specific GPT-4 judge gives a rationale and a 1–10 score in Rating: [[score]] form. The paper uses temperature 0.6 and validates automatic judging on 100 randomly sampled dialogues with five experts and majority human ratings, reporting 87% automatic–human agreement versus 80% internal human agreement. The pinned OpenCompass fork exposes material implementation boundaries: its GPT-4 configuration uses gpt-4-1106-preview at temperature 0.8 rather than the paper's 0.6, and the MR/GR prompts include a reference dialogue/solution path. Its parser takes the first bracketed integer with re.search and performs no 1–10 range check. Unparsed judge outputs are skipped; this shrinks turn and dialogue coverage, a dialogue with no parsed turns disappears, and an all-invalid run asserts. For parsed results, dialogue score is the minimum evaluated turn score and task score is the unweighted mean of dialogue minima. The paper's Avg. is the macro mean of all 13 task scores, but the public summarizer emits only task scores. The old Win Rate metadata was therefore removed because neither the paper's primary metric nor this pinned public scorer computes a pairwise win rate. Formal publication evidence [site-a11q-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 5245×585 (English) and 5245×585 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 5243×583 and 5243×583. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
